title: Quarterly Scenario Lab: Elastic Thresholds & Fiscal Guardrails for Dedicated Autoscale
creator: Ariel Chen
description:
Objective:
Run a focused quarterly scenario lab that defines and validates concrete elastic threshold policies and fiscal guardrails for Dedicated capacity autoscale. The deliverable is a tested, documented runbook that product, infra, and ops teams can execute to safely expand/retract dedicated pools in response to realistic surge patterns while keeping unit economics within targets.

Context and motivation:
- Customers adopt Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation but expect cost predictability. Current autoscale behavior can cause step-cost volatility during short-lived spikes; we need granular thresholds and guardrails that are both safe and cost-aware.
- Previous experiments (see PM-4219 cohort run) showed 12% cost variance during weekday surge windows and flaky canaries under multi-tenant queueing. We must codify learnings into policies and operational playbook.

Scope (what we will ship this quarter):
1) Threshold matrix: a curated set of policy primitives (queue length, percent-utilization, tail-latency, warm-pool-usage) with recommended default cutoffs per SKU family.
2) Fiscal guardrails: burst budget meter and rollback triggers with explicit cost-velocity limits and a soft/hard cap model tied to subscription tiers.
3) Canary plan and experiment harness: an automated simulation harness plus 3 staged canaries (lab, shadow, staged-customer) and success/failure criteria.
4) Runbook & Dashboards: detailed runbook (play-by-play), per-route cost/latency dashboards, and alerting thresholds.
5) Telemetry changes: event labels for autoscale decisions, pre/post scaling histograms, and cost attribution tags.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Reduce median per-customer daily cost variance from autoscale by >= 40% in pilot accounts.
- Keep 99th-percentile latency SLO violation delta <= 5% after scale events.
- Canary failure rate < 2% across staged rollouts.
- Documented runbook accepted by SRE and Finance (sign-offs).

Trade-offs and assumptions:
- We prioritize cost predictability over maximum instantaneous capacity: guardrails may throttle extreme bursts to avoid disproportionate cost.
- Tightening thresholds increases risk of transient latency degradation; that risk is mitigated by prefix/KV caching and prioritized fallback to compatible model variants.
- Fiscal guardrails rely on accurate near-real-time cost telemetry — we assume telemetry ingestion lag <= 90s for safe enforcement.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1-2 (Spike & Design): finalize threshold primitives, economic models, and success criteria. Deliverable: design doc + simulation spec.
- Week 3-5 (Build): implement guardrail service, tagging for telemetry, and simulation harness.
- Week 6 (Lab Run): whitebox experiments in sandbox pools (synthetic and recorded workloads).
- Week 7 (Shadow Canary): apply policies in shadow for 10 pilot accounts with telemetry-only enforcement.
- Week 8-9 (Staged Rollouts): progressive rollout to tiered accounts behind staged gating and finance approvals.
- Week 10 (Wrap & Handoff): finalize runbook, dashboards, and train oncall.

Rollout gating criteria:
- Lab: no more than 10% regression in median latency under synthetic surges.
- Shadow: telemetry matches lab within 15% and no emergency escalations.
- Staged: pilot accounts show < 40% cost variance reduction and no more than 2 P1 incidents.

Monitoring and observability:
- New dashboards: per-pool autoscale decisions, cost-velocity charts, pre/post scale latency histograms. Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/autoscale-policies (placeholder).
- Alerts: alert to SRE on rollback triggers, and Finance on burst-budget breaches.

Cross-team responsibilities:
- Product (Marcus Patel): policy spec, canary acceptance criteria, runbook owner.
- Eng (Omar Haddad, Jin Park): guardrail service implementation, telemetry tagging, simulation harness.
- SRE (Leah O'Connor): canary orchestration and incident playbook integration.
- Finance (Priya Nair): cost model, guardrail budget thresholds, and approval gating.
- DX/Docs (Sofia Martinez): runbook and customer-facing guidance.

Open questions and risks:
- Telemetry lag: if >90s we need an optimistic enforcement mode — requires ENG-19876.
- Multi-region coordination: cross-region capacity handoff may create oscillations; evaluate region-specific thresholds.
- Edge-case workloads (bursty short seq vs long steady seq) may need SKU-specific tuning — we will capture these as sub-issues during lab.

Deliverables:
- policy-matrix.md (final threshold matrix)
- autoscale-guardrail-service (code + API)
- simulation-harness (repo + recorded scenarios)
- runbook.pdf and runbook Confluence page (link below)
- dashboards and alerting configured

Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DA/Elastic+Thresholds+Design (draft)
- Simulation repo (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-sim (work-in-progress)
- Related Linear parent: PM-4219

Notes on cost modeling:
- We will model cost impact using a burst-budget bucket (B tokens) measured against rolling 24h spend. The guardrail enforces a soft surge multiplier (x1.5) and hard cap (x2.5) per commitment tier; Finance to provide exact multipliers for each SKU.
- A small fiscal cushion (2-5% of committed spend) is recommended to reduce false-positive throttles for benign anomalies.

Minimum viable canary plan (MVP):
1) Lab harness with replay of 3 synthetic scenarios (short spike, sustained surge, interleaved multi-tenant)
2) Shadow run for 7 days across 10 pilot accounts (no user-facing changes)
3) Staged rollout to 50 accounts with opt-in and finance approvals

Post-launch ops:
- Weekly review for first 4 weeks: compare predicted vs actual cost delta, and iterate thresholds.
- Quarterly audit: performance, cost, and incidents; incorporate into OKRs for next quarter.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- All deliverables above implemented and verified against KPIs.
- Runbook approved by SRE and Finance.
- Cross-team retrospective and a documented rollback/emergency flow.
